candidate.answerReason: One hour of actual use consumes as much charge as eight idle hours. The phone has spent eight hours idle and one hour in use, consuming 16 of its 24 idle-hour units and leaving eight hours.

methods.label: Measure charge in idle-hour units
methods.explanation:
Measure battery charge in units equal to the charge needed for one idle hour. A full battery contains \(24\) such units. Since a full battery lasts \(3\) hours of actual use, each hour of actual use consumes \(24\div3=8\) units.

The \(60\) minutes of use equal \(1\) hour and are included in the \(9\) hours the phone has been on. Thus the phone has spent \(9-1=8\) hours idle. Its total charge consumption is
\[
8\times1+1\times8=16\text{ units}.
\]
That leaves \(24-16=8\) units. With no further talking, each remaining unit lasts one hour, so the battery will last \(8\) more hours, choice B.
methods.levelReason: Choosing convenient battery units reduces the problem to whole-number rates, time conversion, and subtraction.

Direct proportion supports translating the full-charge lifetimes into hourly consumption; time conversion and parts-and-total reasoning support the remaining steps. The written method uses whole-number battery units and does not require equation modeling or fraction operations.
